messages:
jess: Heads up — noticed our SLA projection numbers in the billing micro-window widget are drifting vs. daily rollups. Projection panel shows 0.7% SLA misses for tenant X but daily aggregate is 2.3%. Anyone seen this before?
omar: Hmm interesting. Is this the new 5m micro-window aggregation? Might be a sampling/rounding artefact. :thinking:
li: I saw something similar last week when we switched to the per-minute tokenization cadence. The micro-window math was truncating fractional compute credits.
ana: @jess can you paste a screenshot or the raw rows? I want to see the event timestamps alignment.
jess: attaching minimal excerpt: ```ts,tenant,window_ms,requests,sla_misses,compute_ms
1705554000000,tenant-x,300000,128,1,23456
1705554300000,tenant-x,300000,140,0,24500```
kevin: Looks like windows are aligned to epoch boundaries, so some heavy requests are straddling two windows. Our per-window SLO calc treats them as separate tiny burns which underestimates misses when you later roll up by tenant.
li: Right — the rollup assumes additive counts, but SLA is a ratio so when you split numerator/denominator across boundaries you get non-linear error.
omar: Short term fix: increase micro-window to 10m for the SLA projection card. That will reduce split bias. Long term: do an exact merge metric where we compute weighted ratios across windows.
ana: Weighted ratios sounds right. But it might be expensive to compute on hover for every tenant in the UI. Could we pre-aggregate a corrected metric server-side?
kevin: We can precompute a "merged_ratio" as part of the hourly job. Formula: merged_ratio = sum(sla_misses)/sum(requests) across N windows. Cheap if we keep incremental sums.
jess: That helps for daily/hours, but the micro-window preview is supposed to be near-real-time for canary rollouts. Precompute latency might add unacceptable lag.
li: Alternative: when computing the card client-side, fetch the raw window sums for that tenant (small payload) and compute merged_ratio in the browser. Minimal CPU and avoids backend churn.
ana: Browser compute would also avoid sampling bias if we return unsampled windows. But we need to ensure the telemetry payload size is bounded. Maybe cap to last 12 windows (1 hour).
kevin: Also want to mention cache savings attribution — if cached responses are returned from the edge, they currently zero-out compute_ms which affects merged_ratio in odd ways. We should annotate cached hits separately and exclude them from SLA denom or show a toggle.
omar: Agreed. UX: add a small "Exclude cache hits" pill on the SLA preview card. Default off for parity with billing.
jess: Action items: (1) li to prototype client-side merged_ratio calc + payload size experiment (2) kevin to add cached-hit flag in telemetry schema (3) marshall a dev note for switching micro-window to 10m in the short term. I'll open a quick RFC.
li: I can mock payload: endpoint `/internal/telemetry/tenant-windows?tenant=tenant-x&n=12` returning small CSV.
nana: One more ask — routing policies: when SLA projection shows potential miss, can we auto-suggest routing to a higher-tier model to reduce latency? Could be a separate feature but related to actionable UX. :rocket:
kevin: Let's keep that as a follow-up. For now I'll start a patch for the telemetry schema.
billing-bot: Note: created ticket #INF-4821 for telemetry schema change and #INF-4822 for client-side merge prototype.
